originalTitle: Fed officials divided on US inflation views; US home prices hit all-time high
simplifiedContent: Here's a simple explanation of the news: The US housing market is very strong, with home prices now higher than they've ever been, making it harder for people to buy homes. At the same time, some important decision-makers at the Federal Reserve (the "Fed") can't agree on what to do about interest rates and inflation. This disagreement is happening while the International Monetary Fund thinks the global economy will grow, but only a little. A drop in demand for oil is also expected, which is the first time that's happened since 2020. This news matters because it can affect the overall health of the economy and the decisions investors make.

originalTitle: Dmart recasts strategy as rapid delivery competition intensifies
simplifiedContent: DMart, a retailer, is changing its strategy because there's a lot of competition in India for delivering goods quickly. To focus on its strongest areas, DMart is stopping its online shopping services in some cities that weren't doing well. The company will now focus on big cities and stick to its approach of keeping costs low and not promising very fast delivery. This decision comes as big companies like Amazon and Flipkart are trying to deliver goods very quickly, which is putting pressure on DMart. DMart is making this change even though its recent earnings weren't very strong.

originalTitle: HDFC Bank, HCL Tech among 143 companies to announce earnings this week
simplifiedContent: This week, 143 companies, including well-known ones like HDFC Bank, Reliance Industries, and HCL Tech, will share their earnings reports. Earnings reports show how well a company did financially during a certain period, in this case, the June quarter. Investors are expecting these companies to show 10% growth, which means they hope the companies made 10% more money than they did during the same time last year. When these reports come out, investors will be paying close attention to see how different industries, like banking and technology, are doing, and what the companies think will happen in the future. This matters because it can affect the stock prices of these companies and the overall stock market.

originalTitle: Indian stock market: How are Sensex and Nifty 50 likely to perform next week amid ongoing US-Iran war?
simplifiedContent: The Indian stock market had a small decline last week, with the Sensex (a measure of the market's performance) falling 0.25% and the Nifty 50 (another measure) falling 0.26%. This means that the overall value of the stocks in these measures went down slightly. The Sensex ended the week at 77,569.39 and the Nifty 50 ended at 24,206.90. This decrease might be related to the ongoing US-Iran conflict, which can affect the market's performance. The market's performance next week will be watched closely to see how it reacts to these global events.
